disposition.reason: Applicants appeal conditions the Williston DRB imposed when it approved a nine-unit planned residential development, including eight new dwelling units (four new single-family houses and two duplexes); this is a municipal appeal about permission for new housing.

discretion.description: Applicants challenged only the DRB's legal authority to impose Condition B (relocating the access road off the wetland) and Conditions F and G (affordable housing); they did not ask the court to delete or modify the conditions or to decide the application on its merits.

evidence.quote: address only the authority of the DRB—and hence, the authority of this Court in this de novo appeal—to impose the contested conditions.
the questions in the Statement of Questions ask the Court solely to determine whether the DRB had the authority to impose the contested conditions.

observed_status.description: The DRB's conditional approval of the nine-unit PRD stands; the court upheld the DRB's authority to impose Condition B and dismissed the challenges to the affordable-housing conditions, and the decision concludes the appeal with final judgment to be entered.

evidence.quote: GRANTED and Applicants’ Motion for Summary Judgment is DENIED on Questions 1 and 2 of the Statement of Questions, in that the DRB has authority to impose Condition B on the 9-unit proposal.
Questions 3 and 4 of the Statement of Questions are DISMISSED, as they raise issues that are beyond the scope of the current appeal.
This Decision and Order appears to conclude both appeals,

judgments.note: Appeal of a DRB approval with conditions of a nine-unit PRD with eight new dwellings; new housing and a municipal appeal. Only the 9-Unit Application parts of the shared decision are used; 117-6-09 concerns the separate 3-Unit Application.

The court repeatedly calls this a de novo appeal (pp. 2, 3, 12, 25). No evidentiary hearing occurred because only legal-authority questions were raised, but the appeal itself is de novo, not on the record.

Filing date not stated. Start: Town's summary judgment motion in this docket dated Oct. 22, 2009 (on_or_before). End: the March 18, 2010 decision, which says it concludes the appeals; the final judgment order effective March 26, 2010 is announced but not observed. 147 days at least.
Eight new units (four single-family houses and two duplexes) stated directly; the existing Hood house is excluded.
The application subdivides the property into two lots, but both contain existing housing and the PRD units' lot arrangement is not stated, so new residential building lots are unknown.

The court says all questions address only the DRB's legal authority to impose the conditions; Applicants did not ask to delete or modify them. Applicants also argued Condition B was arbitrary for lacking a reasonable standard, but the court treated it as premature and the questions remained about authority.
The court states the decision appears to conclude both appeals and that final judgment will be entered; no further review is shown.
Page 11 says the DRB approved on April 28, 2009; footnote 3 refers to April 29, 2009 meeting minutes, apparently a slip since page 2 places the decisions in the minutes of the April 28 meeting.
Contested conditions concern access road relocation (site) and affordability details derived from the applicants' own growth management commitments; none changes the units, size or design.
